site.tagline: A cinematic, RTL-first React design system.
site.description: design-eg is an open-source React design system: contrast-checked design tokens, accessible Radix + Tailwind v4 components, ready-made blocks and page templates, plus a CLI that copies the source into your project.

nav.menuDescription: Every component, block and template in the registry.

home.headline: Build interfaces that feel {accent}.

components.label: Components
components.body: Buttons, fields, overlays, navigation and feedback primitives built on Radix.

blocks.label: Blocks
blocks.body: Composite sections: heroes, pricing tables, data tables, stat grids, filter bars.

templates.label: Page templates
templates.body: Whole screens: sign-in, sign-up, OTP, settings, a dashboard shell and error pages.

tokens.title: Tokens compiled from one seed
tokens.body: A brand is a JSON file. The compiler derives OKLCH ramps, semantic roles for light and dark, and fails the build below WCAG AA.

rtl.title: RTL and Arabic first
rtl.body: Logical properties everywhere, a dedicated font stack per script and tuned line-height. Flip dir and nothing breaks.

source.title: Own the source
source.body: Install from npm or copy components with the CLI. Every item is a shadcn-compatible registry entry.

radix.title: Radix under the hood
radix.body: Keyboard navigation, focus management and ARIA come from Radix primitives. Styling comes from tokens.

home.sampleTitle: This is a sample of the library.

sampleBody.one: The single item has its own page, with a live preview, the source and its dependency list.
sampleBody.other: Every one of the {count} items has its own page, with a live preview, the source and its dependency list.

docsHub.title: Documentation
docsHub.intro: {components} primitives, {blocks} composite blocks and {templates} page templates. Every page previews in whichever theme, brand, language and density you pick in the bar above, because the controls live in the shell rather than in the demo.
docsHub.installCopy: Or copy the source into your project and own it from there:
docsHub.installStyles: Either way, import the stylesheet once, after Tailwind:
docsHub.forMachinesIntro: Everything here is also machine-readable, generated from the same sources as the pages. The URLs are stable.

templatesPage.title: Template gallery
templatesPage.intro: {count} whole pages, each composed only from primitives and blocks in this registry. They are fully controlled: they render and validate, and hand the values back to you rather than navigating by themselves.

button.title: Button
button.description: Six variants, six sizes, loading state and asChild composition. Hover and active colours come from the primary-hover and primary-active tokens, so every brand gets correct feedback for free.

fields.title: Input, Label, Switch
fields.description: Form controls share one height scale (--control-h-*) that reacts to the density switch above. Focus rings use the ring token and keep a 2px offset for visibility on any surface.

card.title: Card
card.description: Header grid with an optional action slot, content and footer. Elevation uses shadow-1 in light mode and a hairline ring in dark mode, the same trick the best dark UIs use.

badge.title: Badge
badge.description: Status colours are separate ramps (success, warning, danger, info) so they never collide with the brand colour, even when the brand itself is red.

demo.skeletonBlurb: Skeletons shimmer with a foreground-tinted gradient.

og.homeAlt: design-eg: a cinematic, RTL-first React design system
og.docsDescription: {components} primitives, {blocks} composite blocks and {templates} page templates. Every one has a live preview, its source, its anatomy and the command that copies it into your project.
og.templatesDescription: Sign-in, sign-up, OTP verification, settings, a dashboard shell and the error pages — each one a registry item you install with a single command and then own outright.

swatches.title: Tokens
swatches.intro: Each brand is one JSON seed. The compiler derives OKLCH ramps, maps them onto semantic roles for light and dark, and fails the build if any text pair falls under WCAG AA.
